blueprint_concepts: Angle bisector, centroid and incentre in vector form
english: A ray of light starts from the point $B(5,1)$ in the $xy$-plane, travels along a straight line and strikes a plane mirror, which is perpendicular to the $xy$-plane, at the point $A(2,-3)$. After reflection the ray passes through the point $C(-3,9)$. The line in which the mirror meets the $xy$-plane meets the $y$-axis at the point $(0,k)$. Then the value of $k$ is ______.
hindi: प्रकाश की एक किरण $xy$-तल में बिन्दु $B(5,1)$ से चलकर एक सरल रेखा के अनुदिश जाती है तथा एक समतल दर्पण से, जो $xy$-तल के लम्बवत् है, बिन्दु $A(2,-3)$ पर टकराती है। परावर्तन के पश्चात किरण बिन्दु $C(-3,9)$ से होकर जाती है। जिस रेखा में दर्पण $xy$-तल को काटता है, वह $y$-अक्ष से बिन्दु $(0,k)$ पर मिलती है। तब $k$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Equal angles with the normal: the normal to the mirror is along the internal bisector of $\angle BAC$, $\hat{u}+\hat{v}=\dfrac{14\hat{i}+112\hat{j}}{65}\parallel\hat{i}+8\hat{j}$
Mirror line: through $A$ with normal $\hat{i}+8\hat{j}$: $(x-2)+8(y+3)=0$, i.e. $x+8y+22=0$

Check with the bisectors of $AB: 4x-3y-17=0$ and $AC: 12x+5y-9=0$: $\dfrac{4x-3y-17}{5}=\pm\dfrac{12x+5y-9}{13}$ gives $x+8y+22=0$ and $8x-y-19=0$; the second contains $\hat{i}+8\hat{j}$, so it is the internal bisector, and the mirror is the other one
solution_full: At the point of incidence the incident ray $AB$ (traced back) and the reflected ray $AC$ make equal angles with the normal to the mirror, on opposite sides. So the normal at $A$ bisects $\angle BAC$ internally, and the mirror line is the other (external) bisector of the angle between the lines $AB$ and $AC$.
Vector form of the internal bisector: its direction is $\hat{u}+\hat{v}$, the sum of the unit vectors along $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$.
The mirror line passes through $A(2,-3)$ and is perpendicular to $\hat{i}+8\hat{j}$: $1\cdot(x-2)+8(y+3)=0$, that is $x+8y+22=0$.
The same result from the angle bisectors of two lines: $AB$ is $4x-3y-17=0$ and $AC$ is $12x+5y-9=0$; their bisectors are $\dfrac{4x-3y-17}{5}=\pm\dfrac{12x+5y-9}{13}$.
The line $8x-y-19=0$ has direction $\hat{i}+8\hat{j}$, so it is the internal bisector of $\angle BAC$ (the normal); the mirror is $x+8y+22=0$.
Check by reflection: the incident direction $\dfrac{-3\hat{i}-4\hat{j}}{5}$ reflected in $x+8y+22=0$ becomes $\dfrac{-5\hat{i}+12\hat{j}}{13}$, the direction of $\overrightarrow{AC}$.
originality_note: New: the mirror is not given; it is recovered from the incident and reflected rays, and the decision between the two angle bisectors is made by the vector sum of unit vectors (way 5). Closest known: equation of the reflected ray for a given mirror; bisector of the angle containing a given point. Different because: the unknown is the mirror, and the correct bisector is the external one, chosen through the unit-vector sum.

concept_use.Angle bisector, centroid and incentre in: Direction of the internal bisector of angle BAC = unit vector along AB + unit vector along AC = (14, 112)/65, which is the normal of the mirror.
concept_use.Angle bisectors: Bisectors of the lines 4x - 3y - 17 = 0 and 12x + 5y - 9 = 0 by equal distances; the one perpendicular to the internal bisector is the mirror.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol and object is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Stated that the mirror is perpendicular to the xy-plane so that its trace is a line and the ray stays in the plane; checked the reflection numerically. Changed: added the perpendicular-mirror clause.
key_step: Seeing that the mirror is the external bisector of angle BAC (normal = internal bisector, from the unit-vector sum).
justification: Routine chain: two unit vectors, their sum, a line through A; the only decision is which bisector is the mirror, settled by the law of reflection. Like 2026-P2-Q17 (L2), an angle question with tangent-direction vectors.
